question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund is evaluating a domicile choice: onshore Mumbai (Cat III) vs GIFT-IFSC (Cat III). On an expected INR 100 crore annual business income from F&O, approximately how much in fund-level income-tax is saved in the holiday year by choosing GIFT-IFSC under Section 80LA (ignore surcharge/cess, use 42.744% vs 0%)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Onshore Cat III fund-level MMR on business income = 100 cr × 42.744% = INR 42.744 crore. IFSC Cat III under Section 80LA with 100% deduction in the holiday year = INR 0. Savings = INR 42.744 crore (rounded). The Trap: A (10 cr) and B (25 cr) understate the MMR stack. D (50 cr) exceeds the 42.744% MMR. Candidates must remember Section 80LA gives 100% DEDUCTION, not a lower rate. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/XIX-E heavily emphasise 80LA economics. XIX-D (Cat I/II) mentions IFSC but less compellingly (pass-through already reduces onshore tax drag). XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) covers IFSC briefly. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before migrating Chambal's strategy to IFSC, map the operating costs — IFSC registration, minimum corpus USD 3 mn, dedicated manager setup, SEZ lease. Net of these, the 40+ point MMR saving usually pays for itself in Year 1 for any fund above ~INR 300 cr AUM. For smaller funds, onshore may still win.
